documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage for Faculty and Student Use in Academic Coursework
documents.stance_why: The policy says faculty 'retain the autonomy to decide appropriate student use of GenAI tools, if any' and requires each syllabus to carry one of two options: 'strictly prohibited' or 'permitted only as explicitly outlined'. It sets no single rule but offers two named options and leaves the choice to instructors, so delegates with tiers.
tiers: Option 1: use of Generative AI is prohibited
Option 2: use is permitted as specified by the faculty member
documents.summary: University-wide Academic Affairs policy requiring each course syllabus to adopt either a prohibition or an instructor-specified permission, with default allowed and prohibited uses when the syllabus is silent. It also allows faculty AI use for course content and licensed-tool grading and sends violations to the Student Academic Conduct Policy.

units.why: The purpose states that 'responsible and ethical integration' of GenAI prepares students for workplaces where AI is 'increasingly prevalent'; it is a career rationale for AI use, so P44 rather than a rule.
units.anchor: prepare students for a world where AI tools in the workplace are increasingly prevalent

units.why: The purpose says policies must preserve the mission 'by fostering academic integrity and promoting critical thinking'; this states the institution-level purpose and principles, so P56. Integrity alone (P95) is only half of it.
units.anchor: preserve the mission of the University by fostering academic integrity and promoting critical thinking

units.why: 'aligning with the associated learning objectives of student coursework and programs' ties AI decisions to learning objectives, which is P83.
units.anchor: aligning with the associated learning objectives of student coursework and programs

units.why: The purpose sentence says the policy 'outlines the expectations for student use of GenAI tools' and faculty responsibilities, setting purpose and scope: P56.
units.anchor: outlines the expectations for student use of GenAI tools in academic coursework
units.frag_end: aid faculty in course related responsibilities.

units.why: Applicability section says the policy 'applies to all University students' and faculty in Academic Affairs and College of Medicine; it defines scope, so P61.
units.anchor: applies to all University students, both graduates and undergraduates

units.why: The definitions section defines GenAI as a subfield 'focused on creating new, original content' and lists tools; a definition that sets coverage (P61).
units.anchor: A subfield of Artificial Intelligence focused on creating new, original content

units.why: 'the University recommends the use of AI tools available within the University's Google-licensed product suite' is a recommendation to use institution-licensed tools, P92 (institution-wide, not one course).
units.anchor: the University recommends the use of AI tools available within the University’s Google-licensed product suite
units.frag_start: Where GenAI use is allowed, the

units.why: Other tools may be used 'if procured through the University's normal procurement guidelines, which includes a thorough security review'; this sets a review/approval requirement before other tools, P65, with academic freedom as the reason.
units.anchor: procured through the University’s normal procurement guidelines, which includes a thorough security review
units.frag_start: As to not hinder academic freedom, GenAI
units.fit_note: Also allows discipline-specific tools, in the name of academic freedom.

units.why: 'Faculty are permitted to use GenAI tools for the development of appropriate course content' is what instructors may use AI for in teaching work, P59, not disclosure or grading.
units.anchor: Faculty are permitted to use GenAI tools for the development of appropriate course content

units.why: 'The faculty member is ultimately responsible to ensure the course material is accurate' makes the instructor accountable for AI-made materials; closest is P48 (review of AI-made course materials), not P59 which is the permission.
units.anchor: ultimately responsible to ensure the course material is accurate
units.fit_note: Requires review for accuracy and learning objectives but says nothing about disclosing AI-made materials.

units.why: 'Faculty are permitted to use authorized university licensed GenAI tools for grading' allows AI grading only with licensed tools, to protect FERPA data; a condition on AI-assisted grading, P101.
units.anchor: permitted to use authorized university licensed GenAI tools for grading purposes
units.frag_start: Faculty are permitted to use authorized

units.why: Other tools may be used for grading 'if purchased through normal university procurement processes, to include a security review and defined data sharing restrictions'; a further condition on grading tools, P101, with the data-protection reason noted.
units.anchor: may be used for grading if purchased through normal university procurement processes

units.why: 'to ensure FERPA-protected student data is not inadvertently released' states the privacy reason for limiting grading tools; its own rule is protecting student data, P50.
units.anchor: ensures FERPA-protected student data is not inadvertently released

units.why: 'Faculty using GenAI tools for grading must ensure grades are accurate and consistently applied as the faculty member is ultimately responsible for assigned grades' keeps a human responsible for grades: P46.
units.anchor: the faculty member is ultimately responsible for assigned grades
units.frag_start: Faculty using GenAI tools for grading

units.why: 'Student graders may utilize GenAI for grading only with explicit direction and approval from the faculty member' sets approval conditions on grading by TAs, P101.
units.anchor: only with explicit direction and approval from the faculty member of record
units.frag_end: member of record for the course.

units.why: 'Faculty members retain the autonomy to decide appropriate student use of GenAI tools, if any' hands the decision to instructors: P04.
units.anchor: Faculty members retain the autonomy to decide appropriate student use of GenAI tools

units.why: 'Any allowed use of GenAI use must ensure course learning objectives are met' conditions instructor choices on learning objectives and college/department limits; P83 fits objectives, and the college-level limit is noted.
units.anchor: must ensure course learning objectives are met
units.frag_start: Any allowed use of GenAI use
units.fit_note: Also says colleges or departments may impose further restrictions (P85).

units.why: 'Faculty must clearly communicate their GenAI policy in their syllabus' requires a syllabus statement: P09.
units.anchor: Faculty must clearly communicate their GenAI policy in their syllabus

units.why: 'explicitly reiterate for each assignment, graded requirement, and evaluation' goes beyond the syllabus to repeat expectations at each assignment; P09 is the nearest, but this repeat-per-assignment rule is separate.
units.anchor: explicitly reiterate for each assignment, graded requirement, and evaluation
units.fit_note: Requires restating expectations at each assignment, not only in the syllabus.

units.why: 'One of the following options ... are required to be included in course syllabi' offers two statements to pick from, i.e. named options for a syllabus; P05 fits as it names categories (prohibited vs permitted as specified).
units.anchor: One of the following options with the recommended statements on the use of GenAI

units.why: Option 1 says GenAI 'is strictly prohibited in this course for any graded assignments or activities', the prohibit default: P01.
units.anchor: is strictly prohibited in this course for any graded assignments or activities
units.frag_start: The use of Generative Artificial Intelligence

units.why: 'All work submitted must be entirely your own original creation' requires submitted work to be the student's own: P29.
units.anchor: All work submitted must be entirely your own original creation

units.why: 'Any unauthorized use of GenAI tools will be processed in the same manner as other academic misconduct violations' classes misuse as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: processed in the same manner as other academic misconduct violations under the University's
units.frag_start: Any unauthorized use of GenAI tools

units.why: Option 2 says use is 'permitted only as explicitly outlined below and for specific assignments', restricting use to listed permissions by assignment: P107 (limit AI to listed tasks) rather than P02.
units.anchor: permitted only as explicitly outlined below and for specific assignments
units.frag_start: The use of Generative Artificial Intelligence

units.why: 'Assignments ... will include clear allowances for GenAI use when assigned' commits instructors to stating allowances at the assignment level; P04 (per-assignment rule) fits better than P35.
units.anchor: will include clear allowances for GenAI use when assigned

units.why: 'Students are responsible for understanding and adhering to these guidelines' makes students responsible for learning the course AI rules: P78.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding and adhering to these guidelines

units.why: 'Any use of GenAI beyond what is permitted ... will be considered a violation of the University's Student Academic Conduct Policy' classes over-permission use as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: Any use of GenAI beyond what is permitted

units.why: 'without proper acknowledgment and disclosure when usage is allowed' counts failure to disclose as a violation, which is P28 (nondisclosure is the violation).
units.anchor: without proper acknowledgment and disclosure when usage is allowed, will be considered a violation

units.why: 'When in doubt, always err on the side of caution and consult with the instructor' tells students to ask before using AI: P10.
units.anchor: always err on the side of caution and consult with the instructor before using GenAI
units.frag_end: before using GenAI on graded assignments.

units.why: Example a lists 'brainstorming and outlining only (with disclosure)' as a sample allowance; it permits brainstorming (P15) with disclosure.
units.anchor: GenAI tools are permitted for brainstorming and outlining only (with disclosure)
units.fit_note: Also covers outlining and requires disclosure.

units.why: Example b lists 'editing and proofreading only (with disclosure)' as a sample allowance: P91.
units.anchor: GenAI tools are permitted for editing and proofreading only (with disclosure)

units.why: Example c says tools are 'encouraged for use (with disclosure and critical evaluation)', an encouraging default option with verification: P02.
units.anchor: GenAI tools encouraged for use (with disclosure and critical evaluation)

units.why: 'GenAI tools can be an effective tool to augment student learning' names a benefit of AI for learning with no rule: P87.
units.anchor: GenAI tools can be an effective tool to augment student learning
units.frag_start: GenAI tools can be an effective

units.why: 'Course specific policies will be included in all course syllabi' states that each syllabus carries the course's policy; communication duty, P09.
units.anchor: Course specific policies will be included in all course syllabi

units.why: 'It is the student's responsibility to fully understand and adhere to this policy and any course-specific variations' makes students find and follow rules: P78.
units.anchor: It is the student's responsibility to fully understand and adhere to this policy

units.why: 'they must seek clarification from their instructor prior to using it' is the ask-first rule for unsure students: P10.
units.anchor: they must seek clarification from their instructor prior to using it for any coursework
units.frag_start: If at any point a student

units.why: 'Unless explicitly stated otherwise by the instructor ... students should assume the following general guidelines apply' is the default when a syllabus is silent: P06.
units.anchor: Unless explicitly stated otherwise by the instructor for a specific course or assignment

units.why: Brainstorming and idea generation is listed under Allowed Uses 'with proper attribution where applicable': P15, with attribution noted.
units.anchor: Using GenAI to explore topics, generate initial ideas, or refine research questions

units.why: Summarization of 'student's own work or publicly available, cited sources' for 'personal study' is allowed; study-aid use, P14.
units.anchor: Condensing information for personal study or to aid in understanding

units.why: 'Using GenAI as a study aid to understand complex concepts, generate practice problems' is allowed; tutor for concepts (P12) and practice problems (P14). I chose P14 since practice problems and study aid lead, but the unit also fits P12.
units.anchor: Using GenAI as a study aid to understand complex concepts, generate practice problems
units.fit_note: Also tutor-style concept explanation (P12) and exploring perspectives.

units.why: 'not for graded assessments unless specified' limits the learning-and-exploration allowance to ungraded use, barring it on graded assessments unless the instructor allows: P19 is the nearest.
units.anchor: not for graded assessments unless specified
units.fit_note: Bars the study-aid use itself on graded assessments, not just submitting AI output.

units.why: 'Translating publicly available content to or from English' is a stated allowed use, which fits writing and language support; closest P91 (editing and writing support), not P18.
units.anchor: Translating publicly available content to or from English
units.fit_note: Translation, which is not editing or proofreading.

units.why: Prohibited: 'Submitting AI-generated content as one's own original work' including 'code', which is P19.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated content as one's own original work

units.why: 'Using GenAI to complete assignments without independent thought or effort' including entire paragraphs or drafts: students must remain the primary problem-solver, P32, though P19 also fits; I chose P32 since the language is independent thought and effort.
units.anchor: Using GenAI to complete assignments without independent thought or effort
units.fit_note: Also bans generating whole paragraphs, sections or drafts (P19).

units.why: 'Using GenAI to gain an unfair advantage or circumvent academic integrity policies' is a ban grounded in fairness; I chose P95 since unfair advantage is the stated reason.
units.anchor: Using GenAI to gain an unfair advantage or circumvent academic integrity policies
units.fit_note: A prohibition, not only a rationale.

units.why: Students 'are ultimately responsible for the accuracy of the content' even when AI is authorized, and 'generating false, misleading, or plagiarized content' is prohibited; verify duty P31 chosen over P74 because the sentence centers on accuracy.
units.anchor: students are ultimately responsible for the accuracy of the content
units.frag_start: Generating false, misleading, or plagiarized content:
units.fit_note: Also bans generating false or plagiarized content (P74, P120) and holds students responsible.

units.why: 'Using GenAI for oral speaking assessments' is banned where speaking skills are assessed, so an assessment-time ban: P22.
units.anchor: Using GenAI for oral speaking assessments, where your speaking skills are being assessed

units.why: 'Using GenAI tools to attend online/hybrid courses where attendance is required' bars AI standing in for attendance; no type covers it, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Using GenAI tools to attend online/hybrid courses where attendance is required
units.uncovered_note: Students may not use GenAI tools to attend online or hybrid classes where attendance is required.

units.why: The graduate thesis section says the policy 'does not provide guidance' for theses and that 'a separate policy will cover thesis and dissertation work'; scope exclusion and research governance, P62.
units.anchor: A separate policy will cover thesis and dissertation work
units.frag_end: Graduate Council and the Graduate School.

units.why: Research guidance comes from the Office of Sponsored Projects and 'should also follow specific agency grant and contract guidelines and/or specific publisher allowances', deferring to funders and publishers: P62.
units.anchor: follow specific agency grant and contract guidelines and/or specific publisher allowances

units.why: Enforcement says unauthorized use 'will be treated as a violation of the University's Student Academic Conduct Policy'; misconduct classification, P36.
units.anchor: Instances of unauthorized GenAI use in coursework will be treated as a violation

units.why: Processing 'using the Academic Misconduct Penalty Record (AMPR)' names the formal record used for reporting, P81.
units.anchor: using the Academic Misconduct Penalty Record (AMPR)

units.why: The header 'Next Required Review: 7/7/2030' states the review cycle; P54.
units.anchor: Next Required Review: 7/7/2030

units.why: 'Responsible Office: Academic Affairs' names the office that owns the policy: P80.
units.anchor: Responsible Office: Academic Affairs

notes: Single university-level document. Thesis and dissertation use is explicitly out of scope. Coder B.
